releases.notes: Dashboard dialogs: name fields validate in the browser again (the name pattern no longer fails to compile), naming the allowed characters. A dialog shows its result and unlocks as soon as the operation answers instead of waiting for the state reload. A non-JSON 5xx from the proxy says the server is not answering instead of asking to sign in again. Dialog errors clear on retry, the submit button shows progress (Capturing…), and notices clear on Cancel and on view or machine switch; a result is shown only where its operation started. Protocol, worker interface 3, catalog schema 7, runtime, guest kernel and host layout 2 are unchanged. Class-1 upgrade: the dashboard restarts alone.

Dashboard keeps keyboard focus on the same machine card or action button when the 5 s refresh rebuilds the lists. Protocol, worker interface 3, catalog schema 7, runtime, guest kernel and host layout 2 are unchanged. Class-1 upgrade: the dashboard restarts; workers and guests are untouched.

Host reserve: each AWS host keeps CPU and RAM box admission never claims, 1 vCPU and 2 GiB on a Host, 0.5 vCPU and 1 GiB on a runner (hostReserveCpuMillis, hostReserveMemoryMib). The host subtracts it from logical CPUs before the vcpuOvercommit ratio and from RAM, for the worker budget, the local controller and runner invitations. The controller/agent unit moves into owcontrol.slice (CPUWeight 1000, MemoryMin/MemoryLow, OOMScoreAdjust -900); the worker and its VMs into owguests.slice (MemoryMax host RAM less the reserve). Every Linux worker also caps OW_MAX_MEMORY_MIB and OW_MAX_VCPUS at host capacity less OW_HOST_RESERVE_CPU_MILLIS/OW_HOST_RESERVE_MEMORY_MIB (default a runner's; ow host up starts its worker with a controller host's) times OW_VCPU_OVERCOMMIT, refuses to start when nothing is left, and starts each VMM with OOM score 500 in a guests cgroup under a delegated worker unit (worker -900, CPU weight 1000, memory.low). apply refuses a reserve that leaves no room for boxes. The worker reports the reserve and ow nodes shows host_reserve (cpu_millis, memory_mib, disk_gib). The node agent builds heartbeats on its status thread and writes its status files on another, so a long capture, a cache hash or a slow disk no longer makes a runner look offline; a beat not refreshed for 1500 s closes the channel. A signal interrupting a worker request (a child process exiting) no longer drops the channel. Class 2 in place: apply stages the units and budget, the normal quiesce/swap/resume upgrade applies them; a running box beyond the lowered CPU budget stays hibernated until capacity frees. A host-to-runner conversion must carry the host's reserve. Protocol, worker interface 3, catalog schema 7, runtime, guest kernel and host layout 2 are unchanged; no stage 0 change.

Dashboard copy and counters for a shared host pool. Footer and sidebar name the shared private host pool; the pool banner says who can see guest data and the invitation policy appears only in the invite dialog. The memory counter shows the owner's provisioned usage against their owner limits (machines, vCPU, memory, disk); the usage view labels pool memory as shared by all users. A failed first state load shows a retry in the machine grid and keeps New machine disabled. Protocol, worker interface 3, catalog schema 7, runtime, guest kernel and host layout 2 are unchanged. Class-1 upgrade: the dashboard restarts alone.

Fork/delete robustness and honest disk admission. Worker disk admission subtracts each box's unwritten bytes (logical size minus allocated blocks), not its full logical size, from real free space, plus the host reserve; status adds free_disk_bytes and unwritten_disk_bytes, shown by ow nodes as disk.free_bytes and disk.unwritten_bytes; cache staging and eviction use the same accounting. A plain snapshot or live fork resumes the guest after the RAM/state save and disk reflink and hashes on a separate worker thread, so other requests are served meanwhile; replies carry timings.paused_ms and timings.total_ms. VMMs boot and load with Firecracker dirty-page tracking; a capture saves only RAM pages changed since that VMM's last boot, load or capture (Diff) and lays them over a reflink of the previous memory image after resume, so published memory files stay complete images; recovery-point chunk seals reuse unchanged memory chunks. A RAM save invalidates the prior base before contacting the VMM; disk-copy, resume or merge failure forces a full RAM save on retry, then incremental captures resume against the repaired base. A live fork of a stopped or hibernated box is refused upfront (controller and worker); a failed fork removes its capture and a failed create its partial directory; delete of an ID the worker never registered removes the directory an interrupted create or fork left, and the controller sends that delete before dropping a never-made machine's row. The worker durably associates a generated live-fork capture with its pending child before capture begins, so deletion after interruption removes both the partial child and its capture, even if the child directory was never created; deletion cancels publication and queued creation, and cleanup errors retain the association for retry. The controller marks a rejected fork's child failed (unmade: true) and releases it, fails an uncertain create or fork its runner still lacks after 30 minutes, and deletes a never-made machine the runner does not list from the catalog only. ow delete names the snapshots that go with a box and asks first (--yes without a terminal); the dashboard delete dialog lists them. Protocol, worker interface 3, catalog schema 7, runtime, guest kernel and host layout 2 are unchanged. Class-2 upgrade: the worker restarts through the existing upgrade policy.

New `ow rename BOX NEW_NAME` (remote API op `rename`, dashboard Rename action) changes only the logical name of a machine its owner holds: physical ID, disk, snapshots, placement, sharing grants, published ports, SSH keys and running state stay, with no worker contact. Owner only; the new name follows the create rules and must be free for that owner; a machine in a move, park, wake or fork transfer refuses it until the transfer ends. Idempotent with --operation-key; renaming to the same name is a no-op. Protocol, worker interface 3, catalog schema 7, runtime, guest kernel and host layout 2 are unchanged. Class-1 controller and dashboard upgrade; no worker restart.

releases.notes: Recovery points read and send only what changed. The worker seals each managed recovery point under the digest of its 8 MiB chunk list (chunks.json beside the manifest; manifest digest sha256-chunks-8m-v1), taking a chunk from the last durable point's seal unread when both files map it to the same physical extents and treating holes as zero chunks; verification of such a snapshot still reads every byte. The uploader sends missing chunks with up to eight parallel in-process signed requests (credentials exported once from the AWS CLI chain), lists the store's chunks once per point in parallel (recorded in RUNNER/recovery-index) instead of checking each chunk, records each upload as it lands so a killed run resumes, and sends again any chunk missing from the store, also for a point whose manifest is already stored. Restores of chunked points download in parallel. Each run prints capture and transfer counts per point. Older readers cannot verify chunk-sealed points; upgrade the CLI used for restore first. New `ow delete-snapshot BOX NAME` deletes one named snapshot through the controller (worker flag snapshot_delete_v1; older runners refuse it before dispatch). Protocol, worker interface 3, catalog schema 7, runtime, guest kernel and host layout 2 are unchanged. Use the normal class-2 worker upgrade; no timer, unit or stage 0 change.

Host staging (first install and ow-host upgrade) installs the pinned release's published Linux ow and, on worker hosts, the newly published ow-guest-linux-amd64, after checking them against the release's SHA256SUMS and source-commit.txt (exact tag and commit); a checksum or commit mismatch is refused before anything is written. A commit that is not the release tag, a missing asset, a non-GitHub repository or --from-source builds on the host as before, and the log names the path. Upgrades run by this or a later ow-host use it; an older ow-host staging this release still builds it. No unit, protocol, catalog, runtime, guest kernel or stage 0 change; no restart.

Opt-in RunnerPool component and controller-host adapter (ow-host pool). New infrastructure only: an unchanged consumer stack gets no new instance and no host replacement; bootstrap.sh, stage 0 and existing Host/Runner resources are unchanged. ow_host.py gains pool-runner identity (node from its data volume) and a join request through a per-instance secret; existing host and runner configs validate and render as before. The controller scaler accepts an opt-in live mode, refused unless a private recovery-drill attestation and a passing provider check for every pool exist; it then makes only newly recorded actions effectful for the adapter to execute and settle by receipt. Shadow configs behave as before. No agent, worker, catalog schema (7, reader floor 7), runtime or CPU ratio change.

Component inputs dataVolumeIops and dataVolumeThroughput set the data volume's gp3 performance; unset keeps the current volume unchanged. EBS applies a size or performance change online, and the host's existing apply step grows the Btrfs filesystem. Component only: runtime, worker and host protocols, catalog schema 7 and reader floor 7, guest kernel, host layout and stage 0 are unchanged; no restart, transfer or guest-state change is required.

Opt-in controller shadow planning with read-only runner inventory refresh, conditional session/placement-bound state and durability observations, and maximum liability forecasts. Only unexecuted shadow forecasts expire at cooldown; effectful or uncertain reservations remain held. Schema 7 and reader floor 7 require private backup and coordinated catalog-reader upgrade. No live provider executor, automatic drain, worker/runtime/guest/kernel/layout or CPU ratio change.

releases.notes: Explicit move and targeted cross-runner fork through durable catalog intents, immutable artifact jobs, prepared imports and conditional commit. Move preserves physical ID, owner/grants and pinned SSH policy; fork refreshes guest/network/SSH identity and belongs to its requester. Explicit pre-commit cancellation/retarget excludes unstarted targets and uses a fresh epoch; post-commit uncertainty stays pinned for forward recovery. Worker interface 3 adds child preparation, durable target exclusion, serialized prepared SSH policy and running-source registration; managed child/exclusion state uses reader-guarded worker state schema 3. Agents accept worker interfaces 1-3; older workers remain fixed-placement and cannot advertise move/fork. Catalog schema/reader floor 5, host protocol 1, runtime, guest kernel and host layout 2 are unchanged. Use the class-2 quiesce/swap/resume upgrade with compatibility checks and explicit cold-memory-loss consent on dedicated eligible runners; no automatic box movement, cold resize, timer, host replacement or infrastructure activation.

Explicit park and coalesced wake through durable catalog transfers and the single fenced hibernation publication scheduler. Park preserves stopped versus hibernated state and releases placement only after verified durable publication; connections wake hibernated boxes, while stopped boxes require explicit start. Warm wake filters the captured runtime, CPU and guest-kernel tuple before reserving a runner. Public host asset downloads hash each opened file instead of trusting metadata cache hits; repeated GET/HEAD requests also incur verification cost. Update controller, dashboard, agents and remote clients; requires the already-installed worker interface 2 placement fences. Catalog schema and reader floor 5, node protocol 1, worker interface 2, runtime, guest kernel and host layout are unchanged from v0.9.10. Retain running worker pins; no worker restart, automatic parking policy, timer, host replacement or implicit cold-memory loss.
